+Feature enhancements:
+
+* [FEATURE #2956](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/2956):
+  Add support for sourcing zsh completions directly, for example, via
+  `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`.
+
 
 14.1.1 (2024-09-08)
 ===================
diff --git a/FAQ.md b/FAQ.md
index 84d01f2..396a029 100644
--- a/FAQ.md
+++ b/FAQ.md
@@ -121,6 +121,19 @@ $ mkdir -p "$dir"
 $ rg --generate complete-zsh > "$dir/_rg"
 ```
 
+Alternatively, for **zsh** only, completions can be sourced directly without
+saving them to a file first:
+
+```
+$ source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)
+```
+
+This is convenient, but note that it is also slower, since it means the
+completion script is regenerated and re-parsed every time you start a new
+shell. If you're sensitive to shell startup time, prefer the approach above
+of generating the completion file once and letting zsh's completion system
+load it (and cache it) on demand instead.
+
 For **PowerShell**, create the completions:

     # anyway to avoid any weirdness
-    ( _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source $1 )
+    #
+    # Note that, since sourcing this file directly no longer calls `_rg`
+    # automatically (that now only happens when it's autoloaded as part of an
+    # actual completion request, courtesy of the dynamic-sourcing support),
+    # we stub out `compdef` (which may not otherwise be defined here, since
+    # we aren't running under a real completion system) and call `_rg`
+    # ourselves afterward.
+    (
+        compdef() { :; }
+        _RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS=1 source $1
+        _rg
+    )
 }

diff --git a/crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh b/crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh
index e9731a1..c73917f 100644
--- a/crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh
+++ b/crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh
@@ -434,7 +434,28 @@ _rg_types() {
   fi
 }
 
-_rg "$@"
+#
+# This script is normally used by placing it (or a symlink to it) in a
+# directory in `$fpath` named `_rg`, where it is autoloaded on demand by
+# zsh's completion system. In that case, `$zsh_eval_context` has
+# `loadautofunc` as its last element while this script is being read, since
+# it's the completion system itself that is triggering the autoload (in
+# order to actually service a completion request), so we go ahead and call
+# `_rg` ourselves.
+#
+# Alternatively, this script can be sourced directly, e.g. with
+# `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`, typically from `.zshrc`. In that
+# case, `$zsh_eval_context` doesn't end with `loadautofunc`, since we're
+# merely being sourced like a normal script and not being autoloaded to
+# fulfil a completion request. So instead of calling `_rg` immediately
+# (which would fail, since `_arguments` can only be called while zsh is
+# actually completing something), we just register it with `compdef` so
+# that it's used the next time completion for `rg` is requested.
+if [[ $zsh_eval_context[-1] == loadautofunc ]]; then
+  _rg "$@"
+else
+  compdef _rg rg
+fi
 
 ################################################################################
 # ZSH COMPLETION REFERENCE
